title: Intracardiac Perfusion with Fixative for Anatomical Studies
author: Janet R Keast
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bahzib76
materials: Make up the following solutions: Perfusion prewash solution: To 300 ml 0.9% sodium chloride (w/v) add 3.75 ml 1% sodium nitrite (w/v) and 0.11 ml heparin (5000 IU/ml). This is made up immediately prior to use. Perfusion fixative: 4% paraformaldehyde in 0.1M phosphate buffer, pH 7.4. This is made up no longer than 48h prior to use, stored at 4C and brought to room temperature on the day of perfusion.

steps.title: Prepare Heart for Perfusion
steps.instruction: Open the chest cavity and perform initial injections and setup.

substeps.instruction: Inject the left ventricle with a mixture of 0.25 ml heparin (5000 IU/ml) and 0.5 ml 1% sodium nitrite
Insert a needle connected to tubing (T-connector to prewash and perfusion solutions) and a peristaltic pump (setting: 50 ml/min) into the left ventricle
Clamp the needle into place using hemostats
Make a small incision in the right atrium to drain blood and perfusate

steps.title: Perform Pre-wash Perfusion
steps.instruction: Perfuse with pre-wash solution until the fluid flowing from the right atrium is clear and the liver and extremities are pale (typically 2-3 min).

steps.title: Perfuse with Fixative
steps.instruction: Perfuse with fixative for a minimum of 10 minutes until organs have stiffened and neural tissues are preserved.

steps.title: Dissect and Post-fix Tissues
steps.instruction: Extract required tissues and continue fixation.

substeps.instruction: Place tissues in fixative for an additional 1h at 4C

steps.title: Wash Tissues
steps.instruction: Wash tissues with phosphate-buffered saline (PBS; 0.1 M, pH7.2).

steps.title: Store Tissues
steps.instruction: Store tissues in PBS containing 0.1% sodium azide at 4C until used for immunohistochemistry or other microscopic analysis.
